results.title: Workload identity for the Reducto API
results.snippet:
tax returns, so we spend a lot of our engineering time on security. We don't use long-lived API keys to call AI models inside Reducto, and now our customers don't need one to call us either, with Workload Identity.

An API key is like a password for a machine. It never expires unless someone remembers to rotate it, so a key pasted into a CI secret in 2023 probably still works. It's a bearer secret, which means whoever has it is you, and it can't tell which machine is using it. And it gets copied into env files, CI settings, Slack messages and logs, each of which is one more place it can leak from.
Rotating keys helps, but you're still storing a secret, just a newer one.

## OIDC and workload identity
Almost always, your code already runs somewhere that knows who it is. A GitHub Actions job knows its repo and branch, and a Kubernetes pod knows its service account. AWS roles, Azure managed identities and Google service accounts know who they are too.

results.title: docs.reducto.ai/parse/overview.md
results.snippet:
> Turn full documents into LLM-ready content: every text block, table, and figure with layout, formatting, and bounding boxes.
Parse is Reducto's foundational endpoint. It reads every page and returns the full document content (text, tables, figures, layout, and formatting) with bounding boxes, then organizes the content into chunks for LLM consumption, RAG pipelines, or downstream extraction.
Each element includes its type, page position, and confidence score. Parse handles multi-column text, nested tables, forms with handwriting, rotated pages, and documents mixing text with charts and images.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Starting December 7, 2026, Parse defaults to r-1. To keep legacy Parse, set `settings.model` to `"legacy"`.
[Reducto parse r-1](https://docs.reducto.ai/parse/r-1.md) is the main Parse model. It combines text, table, figure, layout, formatting, and grounding in one full-page model. Legacy Parse is the previous pipeline.
| Pipeline | Recommended use | How it works |
| - | - | - |
| **r-1** | All new Parse pipelines and most existing workloads | One full-page model handles text, tables, figures, layout, formatting, and grounding together. |

results.title: Reducto MCP Server
results.snippet:
The Reducto MCP server connects AI agents directly to Reducto. Once installed, agents in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, or any other [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) client can classify, parse, extract, split, and edit documents as part of their reasoning loop, without custom integration code.
##
​
Agent quick path
If you are setting this up for a coding agent, choose local MCP for local files and hosted MCP for public URLs.
After setup, ask the agent to call:
```
parse_document(document_url="https://cdn.reducto.ai/samples/fidelity-example.pdf")
```
For local files, ask the agent to call `upload_file("./document.pdf")` first, then pass the returned `reducto://` URL to `parse_document`.
##
​
What is MCP?
The Model Context Protocol is an open standard that lets AI agents call external tools. An MCP server exposes a set of tools (here, Reducto’s APIs) that the agent can invoke as part of its reasoning loop. You install the server once, point your client at it, and the agent figures out which tool to call and how to chain results. results.title: Overview
results.snippet:
Reducto is the agentic document platform for AI teams who need production-grade document processing at enterprise scale. It provides a complete toolkit for the full document lifecycle, from classification and extraction to editing and workflow orchestration, powered by custom in-house and leading frontier models. **What you can build:**
- **Automated intake pipelines** that classify, split, and route documents without manual triage
- **Structured data extraction** from invoices, contracts, medical records, and any document type at scale
- **Document generation and editing** that fills forms, modifies templates, and produces new documents programmatically
- **RAG-ready content pipelines** with layout-aware chunking optimized for LLM consumption
- **Multi-step workflows** that chain classification, parsing, extraction, and editing into single API calls

Read every page into LLM-ready text, tables, and figures, preserving layout and reading order, with layout-aware chunking.

**Agent-ready tooling:** Reducto integrates directly into AI agent workflows via the [MCP server](/mcp-server), [CLI](/cli), and native SDKs.
